HEADACHE CLINIC DOCTOR

By: Latashia Naidoo | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Fall from grace of 'medical pioneer'

Unique Selling Point:
Renowned maxillo-facial surgeon, Dr Elliot Shevel, is facing murder charges in the deaths of two patients who underwent his eponymous 'Shevel Desensitization Procedure'.
The allegations are that his age - he's currently 82 - could've been a contributing factor to his ability to perform the complicated and invasive procedure.

Summary:
World-renowned headache doctor Dr Elliot Shevel is a maxillo-facial and oral surgeon who started The Headache Clinic in 1992, and has served as its medical director ever since. But over the past year, the reputation of the man and his internationally-acclaimed clinic has been in tatters.
Dr Shevel appeared in the Randburg Magistrate's Court in November 2024 following his arrest - charged with the murder of one of his patients - who died hours after receiving treatment at his clinic. Another patient suffered irreversible brain damage that's left him in a permanently vegetative state.
The 81-year-old headache specialist was arrested at his Illovo home, accused of the murder of 38-year-old Marinella Avvakoumides, whom he treated on 15 July 2021.
Shevel is alleged to have performed his eponymous Shevel Desensitisation Procedure on her, which involves injecting the patient with a thick needle at the back of the skull to "permanently numb" pain signals from tendons connecting the neck muscles to the skull.
Shevel is also accused of the death of another patient in 2024, who died under similar circumstances to Avvakoumides.
In September, Shevel was suspended from practicing by the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) amid an investigation into the deaths of his two patients.
Only nine doctors have been suspended, pending the institution of a formal inquiry since 2020, according to the Health Professions Council of SA.
The case continues on 11 March.

Press Release:


Deadly Headaches  

It’s a specialised procedure pioneered by a renowned surgeon – and for decades, it’s relieved patients of debilitating headache pain. But recently, something has gone very wrong. Three patients died, allegedly suffering massive brain and spinal cord damage
in the wake of the procedure – while others claim it’s caused severe, lasting damage. What really happened behind closed doors at this Johannesburg clinic? And how does a celebrated specialist become a murder accused?

Producer: Latashia Naidoo | Presenter: Erin Bates 


Script:


HEADACHE CLINIC SCRIPT - FINAL

UPS PROMO VID
“Dr Shevel leads the world in eliminating migraine, tension headache, cluster headache and more…”

VO: For thousands of people he was a godsend, the pioneer behind revolutionary medical treatments.

UPS SABC: “It’s taken me 20-odd years to get to this stage of constant study and hard work…”

VO: Among the estimated 9 million South Africans with regular headaches, an astonishing 70% of migraine sufferers say they experience mental health issues.

UPS SABC: “…how many South Africans have actually taken to it, have used it, and some of the feedback you’ve received?”
Shevel: ‘Oh my Lord...’

VO: So, it’s unsurprising that by 2015, this specialist headache clinic in Johannesburg was treating as many as 150 new patients each month.

Youtube testimonials:
‘Today I feel a different person…’
‘I look forward to going on and living a normal life…’
‘It’s not just a clinic but a place where people…’

VO: But despite hundreds of testimonials praising his treatments, this is the story of a shattered legacy, and the loved ones of some former patients left to pick up the pieces.

[PAUSE]

VO: It’s about the fall from grace of renowned Maxillofacial Surgeon and founder of The Headache Clinic, Dr Elliot Shevel… now awaiting trial for murder.

UPS from Court:
Strap: Tuesday, 11 March 2025. Randburg Magistrates Court
“My lawyers have told me I’m not allowed to speak to anybody. I’d love to help you, I really would, but I’m sure that when the trial is over you’ll have some really lovely stuff.”

LINK Magistrate’s Court: "Dr Shevel’s court appearance early last month was brief… The Prosecution’s request for a postponement to review documents was granted and for now, no trial date has not been set…. The doctor pleaded NOT GUILTY and is out on R5000 bail."

[PAUSE]

VO: Bruce Johnstone suffered from severe stress-related migraines.
His transformation from an active family man to being paralysed and wheelchair bound is still a painful memory for his eldest son, Tristan, and friend, Chris Wilkinson.

Chris Wilkinson: It was a day that I’ll never forget but a day that I can barely remember

VO: Bruce went to consult Dr Shevel at his Headache Clinic.

TRISTAN CLARKE: He kind of just told me it was a small procedure, nothing too crazy, you know he’ll be in and out and he’ll probably go back to work.

VO: Tristan was 19 at the time.

TRISTAN CLARKE: It was just another normal day. I actually remember the car drive on our way to my college…

VO: But that day in late 2022 would be far from normal for this family…
Bruce collapsed during a procedure at The Headache Clinic and suffered a stroke which left him unable to walk or speak…

Chris Wilkinson: He went for assistance and he left in an ambulance. And that was it.

[PAUSE]

LINK: "Dr Shevel has been practicing medicine for over 50 years. He specialised in Maxillofacial and Oral Surgery which deals with issues related to the jaw, neck, mouth and face."

VO: He later turned his attention to headache and migraine treatments, developing so-called unique procedures to help those suffering from these conditions.

UPS Shevel: "People are coming from all over the world to have this treatment. So, it’s a very exciting time and it’s something that people should know about."

VO: Dr Shevel says his treatments focus on the origins of headache pain – the muscles of the neck and jaw, as well as tendons and small blood vessels on the surface of the skull.

UPS Roedolf video: ‘Draai jou kop soontoe, asseblief. Nog ‘n bietjie. Okay.’ (SUBS DR SHEVEL [Turn your head to the side, please. A bit more. Okay])

VO: This video shows a former patient undergoing the so-called Shevel Desensitisation Procedure, one of the surgeon’s patented treatments.

VO: It involves inserting needles into the pain trigger points, numbing the tendons and blocking pain signals….

Roedolf: He said to me he can cure me, not lighten the load a little bit, have less headaches. He said to me he can 100% cure me.

VO: Roedolf Matthee had his procedure at The Headache Clinic in January last year, but the relief was brief and the migraines returned within 24 hours.
Dr Shevel suggested he undergo a follow-up procedure

Roedolf: So I said to him I’ll come back in three or four months. I have to save up a little money because I don’t just have R25,000 lying around. The medical aid doesn’t cover any of this, by the way.

UPS DR SHEVEL:
"Look there’s no, there’s no medical procedure that can give you 100%. But the results are better than anything else.”

VO:
ON SCREEN
Controversial and mainly experimental.
Lacks robust scientific evidence
no real clinical trials

VO: On his website Dr Shevel lists over 30 published peer-reviewed scientific articles. But there are concerns around the legitimacy of his “near-miraculous” Desensitisation Procedure…

VO: While the surgeons we spoke to wouldn’t go on record, they also raised questions about the apparent lack of substantial clinical trials for this kind of treatment.

VO: And at least one leading medical aid says the treatments offered at the Headache Clinic haven’t met its clinical requirements for medical scheme funding, adding that it only pays for evidence-based interventions.

UPS PROMO VIDEO: “…Dr Shevel and his team at The Headache Clinic will accurately diagnose the source of your pain and guide you on a treatment journey to living your life pain-free.”

Rachelle Roberts: When he came out he had some sort of - I wouldn’t say incisions, but little holes, and there were quite a few. And he, well we had hope that this would be the answer to everything.

VO: Rachelle Roberts’ husband Matt had persistent headaches for years, and underwent the Shevel Desensitisation Procedure in November 2021.

Rachelle Roberts: He wasn’t a changed man, let’s put it that way. But then as soon as the painkillers started wearing off later in the day, then a bit of the headache started coming back and that only got worse.

VO: Five days later, they were back at The Headache Clinic.

Rachelle Roberts: And this time I did go in with him and the exact same procedure was done, with a few more needles being inserted.

VO: Within a few weeks, on Christmas Eve, the pain grew so severe that Rachelle rushed Matt to hospital. Over the next few days his condition deteriorated.

VO: Finally a CT scan revealed the source of Matt’s pain: A tumour at the base of his skull, near his brainstem…

Rachelle Roberts: And then on the 29th, in the morning… I can’t remember if it was around seven or eight, uhm, then Matt passed away, he left us.

UPS Shevel: "One has to have a neurological examination because although the vast majority of headaches and head pain don’t come from the brain it is possible that there’s a brain tumor or meningitis or something that’s life-threatening…"

LINK: "This is a clip from an interview with Dr Shevel just four months before Matt’s treatment at the headache clinic. In his own words: 'it is possible that there’s a brain tumor or something that’s life-threatening'… And yet, even though Matt went for a pre-screening at the clinic, it appears the tumour was not found."

VO: The Johnstone family claims Bruce underwent the very same procedure in November 2022.

TRISTAN: I needed some closure as to, you know, what happened, how did it happen. So I phoned The Headache Clinic and she told me they started the procedure on my dad and about 20 minutes into the procedure my dad had collapsed…

VO: Dr Shevel has denied performing his Desensitisation Procedure on Bruce, but has also refused to give the family any more information… He did, however, refund them almost the entire cost of the procedure…

[PAUSE]

LINK: "For about three decades Dr Shevel treated many people with his somewhat unorthodox, revolutionary procedures… But it seems things started to go wrong four years ago. And it was the death of a former patient, Marinella Avvakoumides, that put the doctor and his clinic in the spotlight…"

Andrew: It was like somebody switched off the sun, like the world was grey; I was like I cannot believe, I cannot believe that I am living this life.

VO: Marinella’s first procedure in June 2021 offered her no relief from her persistent cluster headaches, and a few weeks later she returned to the clinic for a second procedure.

Andrew: From 10 to 12 o’clock this procedure was happening. There was a different series of injections as far as I understand…

VO: Marinella’s brother, Andrew has pieced together the events of that day from her Whatsapp messages to friends and family.

Andrew: It was quite stressful for her. She asked them to open a window and stop. She was either feeling nauseous or sick or whatever… And then something was administered, I don’t know if it was a nausea thing or if it was a painkiller, and then the procedure was continued.

VO: Hours later, Marinella collapsed and lost consciousness on the way to the hospital.

Andrew: They said something like intracranial and intraspinal hemorrhaging and brain and nerve tissue… that’s the words I remember.

VO: Hospital reports show Marinella suffered significant damage to her brain and spinal canal. And was declared brain dead.

[PAUSE]

DR HALL: [...] “We know that medicine is not a risk-free activity, a risk-free discipline – mistakes are made, errors can be made, there are risks, things can go wrong with the best of intentions.”

VO: Dr Susan Hall heads up Stellenbosch University’s bioethics department, which explores ethical, social and legal issues in medicine.
One of the core principles of ethical medical practice is empowering patients to make informed choices.

DR HALL: There’s a great deal of onus on the physician to inform the patient properly. The patient should be informed of all the risks of any given procedure, even if those risks are low.

VO: The Headache Clinic information booklet on the Desensitisation Procedure, only mentions localised skin numbness and infection as possible side effects.

Andrew: We don’t believe that if there were any risks that said you could lose your life as a complication, that my sister would ever have undergone this procedure.

VO: Dr Shevel’s medical license was suspended by the Health Professions Council of South Africa, after Marinella’s death and, reportedly, the death of another of his patients in June last year.

VO: In November he was charged with the murder of Marinella Avvakoumides.

[PAUSE]

VO: Questions around Dr Shevel’s procedures, his age and what exactly happened at The Headache Clinic over the past few years may never be fully answered.

VO: But it’s hoped that the court process will provide these former patients and their families with much-needed closure.

END.


PROMOS:

PROMO 1
VO: Once a celebrated medical specialist

UPS Roedolf:
"He said to me he can cure me, not lighten the load a little bit, have less headaches. He said to me he can 100% cure me."

VO: Now, a dark shadow has been cast on the doctor and his clinic… and some former patients want answers.

UPS Chris Wilkinson:
"He went for assistance and left in an ambulance. And that was it."

PROMO 2
VO: In the winter of 2021, Marinella Avvakoumides was rushed to hospital…

UPS ANDREW: "It was like somebody switched off the sun, like the world was grey; I was like I cannot believe, I cannot believe that I am living this life.”

VO: Now, the doctor who treated her with his unique and somewhat unorthodox procedures is under the spotlight…

PROMO 3

UPS CHRIS
"It was a day that I’ll never forget but a day that I can barely remember…"

VO: An active family man and father of three… allegedly paralysed after a simple procedure to treat his headaches…

UPS TRISTAN
"It was really tough and the first thing that also came to mind is what about my brothers… What Am I going to do here?"

procedure pioneered by a renowned surgeon – and for decades, it’s relieved patients of debilitating headache pain. But recently, something has gone very wrong. Three patients died, allegedly suffering massive brain and spinal cord damage in the wake of the procedure – while others claim it’s caused severe, lasting damage. What really happened behind closed doors at this Johannesburg clinic? And how does a celebrated specialist become a murder accused? Producer: Latashia Naidoo | Presenter: Erin Bates Script: HEADACHE CLINIC SCRIPT - FINAL UPS PROMO VID “Dr Shevel leads the world in eliminating migraine, tension headache, cluster headache and more…” VO: For thousands of people he was a godsend, the pioneer behind revolutionary medical treatments. UPS SABC: “It’s taken me 20-odd years to get to this stage of constant study and hard work…” VO: Among the estimated 9 million South Africans with regular headaches, an astonishing 70% of migraine sufferers say they experience mental health issues. UPS SABC: “…how many South Africans have actually taken to it, have used it, and some of the feedback you’ve received?” Shevel: ‘Oh my Lord...’ VO: So, it’s unsurprising that by 2015, this specialist headache clinic in Johannesburg was treating as many as 150 new patients each month. Youtube testimonials: ‘Today I feel a different person…’ ‘I look forward to going on and living a normal life…’ ‘It’s not just a clinic but a place where people…’ VO: But despite hundreds of testimonials praising his treatments, this is the story of a shattered legacy, and the loved ones of some former patients left to pick up the pieces. [PAUSE] VO: It’s about the fall from grace of renowned Maxillofacial Surgeon and founder of The Headache Clinic, Dr Elliot Shevel… now awaiting trial for murder. UPS from Court: Strap: Tuesday, 11 March 2025. Randburg Magistrates Court “My lawyers have told me I’m not allowed to speak to anybody. I’d love to help you, I really would, but I’m sure that when the trial is over you’ll have some really lovely stuff.” LINK Magistrate’s Court: "Dr Shevel’s court appearance early last month was brief… The Prosecution’s request for a postponement to review documents was granted and for now, no trial date has not been set…. The doctor pleaded NOT GUILTY and is out on R5000 bail." [PAUSE] VO: Bruce Johnstone suffered from severe stress-related migraines. His transformation from an active family man to being paralysed and wheelchair bound is still a painful memory for his eldest son, Tristan, and friend, Chris Wilkinson. Chris Wilkinson: It was a day that I’ll never forget but a day that I can barely remember VO: Bruce went to consult Dr Shevel at his Headache Clinic. TRISTAN CLARKE: He kind of just told me it was a small procedure, nothing too crazy, you know he’ll be in and out and he’ll probably go back to work. VO: Tristan was 19 at the time. TRISTAN CLARKE: It was just another normal day. I actually remember the car drive on our way to my college… VO: But that day in late 2022 would be far from normal for this family… Bruce collapsed during a procedure at The Headache Clinic and suffered a stroke which left him unable to walk or speak… Chris Wilkinson: He went for assistance and he left in an ambulance. And that was it. [PAUSE] LINK: "Dr Shevel has been practicing medicine for over 50 years. He specialised in Maxillofacial and Oral Surgery which deals with issues related to the jaw, neck, mouth and face." VO: He later turned his attention to headache and migraine treatments, developing so-called unique procedures to help those suffering from these conditions. UPS Shevel: "People are coming from all over the world to have this treatment. So, it’s a very exciting time and it’s something that people should know about." VO: Dr Shevel says his treatments focus on the origins of headache pain – the muscles of the neck and jaw, as well as tendons and small blood vessels on the surface of the skull. UPS Roedolf video: ‘Draai jou kop soontoe, asseblief. Nog ‘n bietjie. Okay.’ (SUBS DR SHEVEL [Turn your head to the side, please. A bit more. Okay]) VO: This video shows a former patient undergoing the so-called Shevel Desensitisation Procedure, one of the surgeon’s patented treatments. VO: It involves inserting needles into the pain trigger points, numbing the tendons and blocking pain signals…. Roedolf: He said to me he can cure me, not lighten the load a little bit, have less headaches. He said to me he can 100% cure me. VO: Roedolf Matthee had his procedure at The Headache Clinic in January last year, but the relief was brief and the migraines returned within 24 hours. Dr Shevel suggested he undergo a follow-up procedure Roedolf: So I said to him I’ll come back in three or four months. I have to save up a little money because I don’t just have R25,000 lying around. The medical aid doesn’t cover any of this, by the way. UPS DR SHEVEL: "Look there’s no, there’s no medical procedure that can give you 100%. But the results are better than anything else.” VO: ON SCREEN Controversial and mainly experimental. Lacks robust scientific evidence no real clinical trials VO: On his website Dr Shevel lists over 30 published peer-reviewed scientific articles. But there are concerns around the legitimacy of his “near-miraculous” Desensitisation Procedure… VO: While the surgeons we spoke to wouldn’t go on record, they also raised questions about the apparent lack of substantial clinical trials for this kind of treatment. VO: And at least one leading medical aid says the treatments offered at the Headache Clinic haven’t met its clinical requirements for medical scheme funding, adding that it only pays for evidence-based interventions. UPS PROMO VIDEO: “…Dr Shevel and his team at The Headache Clinic will accurately diagnose the source of your pain and guide you on a treatment journey to living your life pain-free.” Rachelle Roberts: When he came out he had some sort of - I wouldn’t say incisions, but little holes, and there were quite a few. And he, well we had hope that this would be the answer to everything. VO: Rachelle Roberts’ husband Matt had persistent headaches for years, and underwent the Shevel Desensitisation Procedure in November 2021. Rachelle Roberts: He wasn’t a changed man, let’s put it that way. But then as soon as the painkillers started wearing off later in the day, then a bit of the headache started coming back and that only got worse. VO: Five days later, they were back at The Headache Clinic. Rachelle Roberts: And this time I did go in with him and the exact same procedure was done, with a few more needles being inserted. VO: Within a few weeks, on Christmas Eve, the pain grew so severe that Rachelle rushed Matt to hospital. Over the next few days his condition deteriorated. VO: Finally a CT scan revealed the source of Matt’s pain: A tumour at the base of his skull, near his brainstem… Rachelle Roberts: And then on the 29th, in the morning… I can’t remember if it was around seven or eight, uhm, then Matt passed away, he left us. UPS Shevel: "One has to have a neurological examination because although the vast majority of headaches and head pain don’t come from the brain it is possible that there’s a brain tumor or meningitis or something that’s life-threatening…" LINK: "This is a clip from an interview with Dr Shevel just four months before Matt’s treatment at the headache clinic. In his own words: 'it is possible that there’s a brain tumor or something that’s life-threatening'… And yet, even though Matt went for a pre-screening at the clinic, it appears the tumour was not found." VO: The Johnstone family claims Bruce underwent the very same procedure in November 2022. TRISTAN: I needed some closure as to, you know, what happened, how did it happen. So I phoned The Headache Clinic and she told me they started the procedure on my dad and about 20 minutes into the procedure my dad had collapsed… VO: Dr Shevel has denied performing his Desensitisation Procedure on Bruce, but has also refused to give the family any more information… He did, however, refund them almost the entire cost of the procedure… [PAUSE] LINK: "For about three decades Dr Shevel treated many people with his somewhat unorthodox, revolutionary procedures… But it seems things started to go wrong four years ago. And it was the death of a former patient, Marinella Avvakoumides, that put the doctor and his clinic in the spotlight…" Andrew: It was like somebody switched off the sun, like the world was grey; I was like I cannot believe, I cannot believe that I am living this life. VO: Marinella’s first procedure in June 2021 offered her no relief from her persistent cluster headaches, and a few weeks later she returned to the clinic for a second procedure. Andrew: From 10 to 12 o’clock this procedure was happening. There was a different series of injections as far as I understand… VO: Marinella’s brother, Andrew has pieced together the events of that day from her Whatsapp messages to friends and family. Andrew: It was quite stressful for her. She asked them to open a window and stop. She was either feeling nauseous or sick or whatever… And then something was administered, I don’t know if it was a nausea thing or if it was a painkiller, and then the procedure was continued. VO: Hours later, Marinella collapsed and lost consciousness on the way to the hospital. Andrew: They said something like intracranial and intraspinal hemorrhaging and brain and nerve tissue… that’s the words I remember. VO: Hospital reports show Marinella suffered significant damage to her brain and spinal canal. And was declared brain dead. [PAUSE] DR HALL: [...] “We know that medicine is not a risk-free activity, a risk-free discipline – mistakes are made, errors can be made, there are risks, things can go wrong with the best of intentions.” VO: Dr Susan Hall heads up Stellenbosch University’s bioethics department, which explores ethical, social and legal issues in medicine. One of the core principles of ethical medical practice is empowering patients to make informed choices. DR HALL: There’s a great deal of onus on the physician to inform the patient properly. The patient should be informed of all the risks of any given procedure, even if those risks are low. VO: The Headache Clinic information booklet on the Desensitisation Procedure, only mentions localised skin numbness and infection as possible side effects. Andrew: We don’t believe that if there were any risks that said you could lose your life as a complication, that my sister would ever have undergone this procedure. VO: Dr Shevel’s medical license was suspended by the Health Professions Council of South Africa, after Marinella’s death and, reportedly, the death of another of his patients in June last year. VO: In November he was charged with the murder of Marinella Avvakoumides. [PAUSE] VO: Questions around Dr Shevel’s procedures, his age and what exactly happened at The Headache Clinic over the past few years may never be fully answered. VO: But it’s hoped that the court process will provide these former patients and their families with much-needed closure. END. PROMOS: PROMO 1 VO: Once a celebrated medical specialist UPS Roedolf: "He said to me he can cure me, not lighten the load a little bit, have less headaches. He said to me he can 100% cure me." VO: Now, a dark shadow has been cast on the doctor and his clinic… and some former patients want answers. UPS Chris Wilkinson: "He went for assistance and left in an ambulance. And that was it." PROMO 2 VO: In the winter of 2021, Marinella Avvakoumides was rushed to hospital… UPS ANDREW: "It was like somebody switched off the sun, like the world was grey; I was like I cannot believe, I cannot believe that I am living this life.” VO: Now, the doctor who treated her with his unique and somewhat unorthodox procedures is under the spotlight… PROMO 3 UPS CHRIS "It was a day that I’ll never forget but a day that I can barely remember…" VO: An active family man and father of three… allegedly paralysed after a simple procedure to treat his headaches… UPS TRISTAN "It was really tough and the first thing that also came to mind is what about my brothers… What Am I going to do here?"

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Renowned maxillo-facial surgeon, Dr Elliot Shevel, is facing murder charges in the deaths of two patients who underwent his eponymous 'Shevel Desensitization Procedure'. The allegations are that his age - he's currently 82 - could've been a contributing factor to his ability to perform the complicated and invasive procedure.
metadata.Summary: World-renowned headache doctor Dr Elliot Shevel is a maxillo-facial and oral surgeon who started The Headache Clinic in 1992, and has served as its medical director ever since. But over the past year, the reputation of the man and his internationally-acclaimed clinic has been in tatters. Dr Shevel appeared in the Randburg Magistrate's Court in November 2024 following his arrest - charged with the murder of one of his patients - who died hours after receiving treatment at his clinic. Another patient suffered irreversible brain damage that's left him in a permanently vegetative state. The 81-year-old headache specialist was arrested at his Illovo home, accused of the murder of 38-year-old Marinella Avvakoumides, whom he treated on 15 July 2021. Shevel is alleged to have performed his eponymous Shevel Desensitisation Procedure on her, which involves injecting the patient with a thick needle at the back of the skull to "permanently numb" pain signals from tendons connecting the neck muscles to the skull. Shevel is also accused of the death of another patient in 2024, who died under similar circumstances to Avvakoumides. In September, Shevel was suspended from practicing by the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) amid an investigation into the deaths of his two patients. Only nine doctors have been suspended, pending the institution of a formal inquiry since 2020, according to the Health Professions Council of SA. The case continues on 11 March.
